extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, and policymakers interested in social media platforms
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive encyclopedic overview of TikTok's policies, moderation practices, privacy/data practices, platform features (like heating and STEM feed), and societal impacts. Covers examples, controversies, and measures the company has taken or proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEM feed safety and reliability checks
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok introduced a dedicated feed for science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) content. It works with Common Sense Networks to check for safety and age appropriateness and with the Poynter Institute for reliability of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnerships with third-party organizations are used to evaluate safety/age-appropriateness and information reliability for specialized content feeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heating (manual promotion) policy and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'heating' tool allows TikTok to manually promote certain videos, comprising 1–2% of daily views; used to grow/diversify content and promote brands/artists/NGOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice intended to boost content not naturally surfaced by algorithm; concerns include employee abuse promoting personal accounts and discretion in approval. TikTok states only a few individuals can approve heating in the US and such promotions take up less than 0.002% of user feeds; negotiations with CFIUS may require heating be performed by vetted US personnel and audited by third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited topics under internal censorship guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal guidelines against the promotion of violence, separatism, and 'demonization of countries' that could be used to prohibit content related to events/subjects such as the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests, Falun Gong, human rights in Tibet, Taiwan, Chechnya, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list of specific sensitive topics and banned criticisms of world leaders indicates broad, sometimes politically-influenced content restrictions; these have been criticized as non-transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppression instructions based on appearance or socioeconomic status
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok moderators were instructed to suppress posts from 'For You' recommendations if the users shown were deemed 'too ugly, poor, or disabled'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal moderation guidance reportedly included discriminatory suppression criteria, raising concerns about fairness and bias in recommendation suppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional restrictions on sexual content and LGBT material
rubrics_metrics.description: The consumption of alcohol, full or partial nudity, LGBT, and intersex contents were restricted even in places where they are legal. TikTok apologized and instituted a ban against anti-LGBTQ ideology (on TikTok), while censorship continues on Douyin due to Chinese regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content allowed or restricted varies by region and platform variant (TikTok vs Douyin); company-level apologies and policy changes may not apply universally because of local legal/regulatory constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Douyin-specific content prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Douyin guidelines forbid live broadcasting by unregistered foreigners, 'feudal superstition', 'money worship', smoking and drinking, competitive eating by the 'already obese', 'toxic' slime, 'pornographic' ASMR such as ear-licking, and female anchors wearing revealing clothes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localized rules reflect domestic regulatory and cultural norms; Douyin policies are customized for the Chinese market and differ significantly from TikTok's global guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency via external expert access
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok said it is granting some outside experts access to the platform's anonymized data sets and protocols, including filters, keywords, criteria for heating, and source code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing anonymized datasets and access to protocols is positioned as a transparency measure; scope and sufficiency of access have been scrutinized and debated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic content detection and blacklisting
rubrics_metrics.description: A shocking beheading video was put on TikTok's blacklist, which detects it before being uploaded. TikTok has worked to remove graphic content, including suicides and other violent imagery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-upload detection/blacklisting is used to prevent known graphic material from being posted; removal and blacklisting are reactive and preventive moderation tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misinformation policies and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok has banned Holocaust denial and removed videos containing COVID-19 misinformation (e.g., Plandemic); it has added links to accurate COVID-19 information and created an Elections Center to combat election misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy actions include content removal, labeling/adding information links, and building in-app resources (Elections Center); effectiveness and coverage have been measured and criticized in independent analyses (e.g., NewsGuard).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extremist and hate speech moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok removed accounts posting ISIL propaganda and execution videos, blocked search terms for neo-Nazi propaganda, and removed content promoting Holocaust denial and calls to violence; yet extremist/hateful content has still circulated and been amplified by algorithmic recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts include account removals, search-term blocking, and takedowns, but platform algorithm dynamics and moderation evasion (e.g., remixing audio) complicate enforcement; calls exist for tighter restrictions and parental controls to protect younger users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits and actions on coordinated inauthentic behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok reported removing large numbers of fake accounts, fake followers, impersonating accounts, videos violating civic integrity/disinformation rules, and dismantled coordinated networks promoting pro-Russian politicians and attempting to discredit governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform enforcement involves removal of accounts and network takedowns, blocking fake likes/follow requests, and preventing spam account creation; partnerships with electoral bodies and fact-checkers supplement these actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age-related safety controls (teenage mode and defaults)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teenage mode shows only whitelisted content, bans pranks, superstition, certain dances and pro-LGBT content (on Douyin), mandatory screen time limits for users under 14, requirement to link accounts to a real identity, and default screen time limits for users under 18 with parental passcodes needed for under-13s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age-gating, time limits, parental-managed privacy settings, and account identity verification are used to limit minors' exposure; enforcement and regional variation (e.g., Douyin) affect implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underage live-streaming and direct messaging restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok forbade direct messaging for users younger than 16 in certain measures and raised the minimum age for livestreaming from 16 to 18 after investigations found children in vulnerable contexts livestreaming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform changes were made in response to safety investigations; age thresholds for features are adjusted to reduce exploitation risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy data collection disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok's privacy policy lists that the app collects usage information, IP addresses, a user's mobile carrier, unique device identifiers, keystroke patterns, and location data; also infers user interests and collects content created by users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive telemetry and behavioral inference are core to the platform; disclosures have been criticized as vague and problematic in jurisdictions lacking robust privacy laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking of non-users and cross-site data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok is able to track information about web users even if they are not users of the TikTok app, including IP address, online browsing habits and web search history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform tracking beyond registered users expands data collection footprint and has regulatory and privacy implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biometric data potential collection
rubrics_metrics.description: In June 2021, TikTok updated its privacy policy to include potential collection of biometric data, including 'faceprints and voiceprints', for special effects and other purposes, stating user authorization would be requested if local law demands such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biometric collection is conditional and depends on local legal requirements and user authorization; experts flagged vagueness and potential problems for some jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing within corporate group and employee access controls
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok can share data with its corporate group, including ByteDance. The company says it employs access control and approval process overseen by a US-based team, but leaked reports indicated some employees in China had access to overseas data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corporate-level data sharing and employee access rights are central privacy risk points; stated mitigations include access controls and US-based oversight, but leaks and investigations challenge completeness of safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data localization and Project Texas safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Texas focuses on unauthorized access, state influence, and software security by siloing privileged US user data within the United States under oversight (TikTok US Data Security Inc. - USDS). Oracle would review/spot check data flows, digitally sign software code, approve updates, oversee content moderation/recommendation, and physical locations would be established for reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data residency, third-party code signing and oversight, and physical review facilities are presented as technical and organizational controls to limit foreign access and address national security concerns; critics and regulators continue to assess adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetization eligibility and revenue sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Creators that have a video reach the top 4% of the platform and have more than 100,000 followers are eligible to receive 50% of its ad revenue. The Creator Fund was replaced with the Creator Rewards Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetization criteria are quantitative (reach percentile and follower thresholds) and determine eligibility and revenue splits for creators; program changes over time affect creator incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influencer sponsorship disclosure expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports that some influencers paid by FeetFinder did not disclose their videos were ads; FeetFinder said it suggested influencers be upfront about who was funding them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent disclosure of sponsored content is an expected ethical/legal practice; failure to disclose has been highlighted as a problematic anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation evasion techniques and platform response
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixing audio or using text-to-video AI models has been used to evade content moderation (e.g., added music to Hitler speeches, or AI-generated violent dehumanizing videos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform must continuously adapt detection techniques as creators and bad actors use editing, remixing, or AI-generation to bypass moderation; examples show moderation is reactive and adversarial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of platform for civic and political communication (Elections Centers and partnerships)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok created in-app Election Centers in multiple languages and partnered with the National Association of Secretaries of State and other organizations to provide accurate local information and combat misinformation around elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Building in-app civic information hubs and partnering with official organizations are measures to reduce misinformation and inform users during elections; their reach and effectiveness vary by region and uptake.
